name: Hair threading (irun kiko)
what_people_do: Wrap sections of hair in black or coloured thread from root to tip to stretch and style it, often for girls and women.
why_they_say_it_works: It keeps hair stretched without heat, protects the ends and looks neat for weeks.

documented_by.source: 'African hair threading', Wikipedia (opened 12 Nov 2026; cites Mensah 2020 and magazines)
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Wikipedia (not a primary source): threading is prevalent across sub-Saharan Africa, especially West and Central Africa; names include Irun Kiko (Yoruba), isi owu (Igbo), Akweley Waabii (Ga); described as a protective style. Cites a 2020 book and magazine pieces.

evidence.tested: Threading for hair length or breakage
evidence.finding: My search found no study of threading. The closest evidence is tight-style traction alopecia (see plaiting entry).

source.name: agent4-traditional-practices.md, 12 Nov 2026 (research file in this project)

harm_note: Tight threading pulls on the roots, so the traction-alopecia warning applies (extrapolated from braids, not threading-specific).
gaps: Origin dates conflict across sources (a popular 15th-century claim, a thesis calling it recent).
